routes.name: Request login OTP
routes.auth: None (before login)
summary: **Request login OTP.** First login step: normalises the phone number, runs abuse checks, stores the number and queues sending of the OTP by SMS. The app then calls /V1/sessions/verify_number_login_v1 with the OTP.
Personal data: Phone (reads / writes) — through the app’s PII integration.
OTP validation and sending run in a background job, so a valid-length number normally gets status: true even if the SMS is later blocked.
headers: macOS/Windows with android/ios device_type is blocked.
curl:
curl -i --request POST "https://testa2.aisle.co/V1/sessions/login_with_phone_number" \
  --header "device_type: ${DEVICE_TYPE}" \
  --header "app_version: ${APP_VERSION}" \
  --header "unique_identifier: ${DEVICE_UUID}" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-binary @- <<JSON
{
  "phone_number": "+911000000001",
  "consent_granted": true,
  "signature_v1": "<app signature>"
}
JSON

steps.explain: Splits phone_number into phone_code / mobile_number / phone_code_id / combined_number (strips a leading 0 and non-digits).
Abuse checks; blocked attempts are logged to MongoDB and answered 403 (ASN check production only; banned check iOS/web only).
Checks number length for the country; finds or creates the sms_notification_phone_numbers row (also copied to MongoDB).
Validates number, SMS signature and daily country limit; sets the OTP in Redis.
Sends the OTP through the selected SMS provider and writes SQL + MongoDB SMS logs (skipped for test numbers).

stores.what: Phone code id + number, consent time.
Number copy; blocked-request log with phone and request headers.

stores.object: OTP data per number, used signatures

stores.what: When a country hits its daily SMS limit.

notes.title: From code — confirm with Dev
notes.text: Documented from the Aisle code @004e72c (`config/routes.rb:168` → `v1/sessions#login_with_phone_number`). No Dev API document lists this route and staging behaviour has not been observed yet; Dev answers and staging observations win where they differ.

notes.title: Request fields
notes.text: `phone_number` — Full number with country code, e.g. +911000000001 (option A); `mobile_number` — Number without code (option B, with phone_code or phone_code_id); `phone_code` — Country code, e.g. +91 (option B); `phone_code_id` — Country code id (defaults to India); in production '1' is treated as missing; `consent_granted` — Stored as first_consented_at on a new number; `signature_v1` — Encrypted app signature; must verify or no SMS is sent; `login_type` — Selects which signature format is decoded.

notes.title: Status codes
notes.text: **200** OTP queued (status: true) or wrong number (status: false); banned iOS device: {is_banned: true, status: false, zendesk_url}. · **403** Blocked request: {message: 'Too many login attempts.'} (country pair, suspicious headers or blocked ASN). · **500** Unhandled error ({title, message, is_backend_error: true}).

notes.title: Example response
notes.text: `{"status": true, "message": "", "phone_code": "+91", "mobile_number": "1000000001", "zendesk_url": "https://support.example.test", "your_story_form_url": "https://forms.example.test"}`

notes.title: Good to know
notes.text: Test numbers (TestPhoneNumber list) skip length/validity checks, ASN check and the real SMS. When an OTP was generated less than MIN_TIME_GAP_BETWEEN_OTPS ago, no new SMS is sent.

notes.title: Per-app
notes.text: The country-pair block uses app_name 'Aisle' (sessions_controller.rb:87).

}
